Loan-book momentum is intact; risk/reward is balanced
Rating: Neutral. Our INR 160 12-month price target is based on 8.2x FY28E EPS of
INR 19.48. Against the INR 169.14 NSE close on 9 November 2026, this implies 5.4%
downside and remains inside our Neutral band of -10% to +15%.
HUDCO's H1 FY27 operating revenue grew 26% year-on-year, its loan book reached
INR 1.86 lakh crore, and gross/net NPAs were 0.71%/0.044%. The core attraction is a
government-linked infrastructure-finance franchise with low impaired assets and a
strong capital buffer. The central valuation question is whether elevated loan growth
can persist without further margin pressure or regulatory friction.
We forecast FY27E-FY29E operating-revenue growth of 23%/13%/12% and EPS of
INR 16.48/19.48/22.48. FY26 reported EPS benefited from a INR 1,459 crore
deferred-tax credit, so we do not extrapolate its 20.15 per-share result mechanically.
Our ordinary tax-rate base case makes FY27E EPS lower before growth resumes.
Catalysts: execution on high-value state MoUs, further NPA resolutions and a stable
funding-cost path. Risks: slower sanctions/disbursements, treasury or FX volatility,
policy-linked asset concentration, and governance/compliance developments. At 30
September, HUDCO disclosed no independent directors against a stated requirement

Forecast framework, catalysts and risk markers
The lending franchise has high government-agency exposure, stated funding diversification and strong reported asset quality. Yet H1
FY27 cost of funds was 7.07% versus 7.04% a year earlier, while yield on loans fell to 8.83% from 9.12%. We forecast a broadly
contained, rather than expanding, margin structure and value FY28E earnings at 8.2x.
A faster conversion of sanctioned projects into disbursements, resolution/recovery of legacy impaired accounts, successful scale-up of
UiWIN/PPP financing, or a lower cost of funds could improve earnings or support a higher multiple.
Slower state/ULB project execution, higher funding costs, unexpected ECL charges, foreign-currency/derivative volatility, or a decline
in capital adequacy would weaken the case. We also flag the disclosure that HUDCO had not fully met conditions linked to its RBI
NBFC-IFC registration at 31 March 2026 and had sought an extension; and the 30 September disclosure of nil independent directors
against the cited requirement of five.
